tool_input.description: Force push local version to remote

result:
The regular push fails because the branches have diverged and the force push is blocked by a security policy. Since you need your tested version on remote, here are your options:

**Option 1:** Pull their changes, resolve the conflict to keep yours, then push normally:
```
git pull origin main
# This will show you both versions, keep yours (your .gitignore wins)
git push origin main
```

**Option 2:** If you want to completely discard their commit and keep only yours, you'd need to ask someone with override permissions to reset the remote branch, since the guard blocks direct force pushes.

**Option 3:** Create a new branch with your work, push that, then have someone update main to point to it.

Which approach works best for your situation? Given that the remote has just one commit (`hotfix: patch the rounding bug`) that you don't want, pulling and keeping yours is probably simplest.
